author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Israel’s military said Friday that a senior Hamas commander was killed in an airstrike in Gaza a day earlier, as bombing continued despite U.S.-backed efforts to restore a 2025 ceasefire.

Hamas’s armed wing confirmed the death of Mohammed Abdel Salam al-Yazouri. The group said he played a prominent role in planning the October 7, 2023 attacks on Israel that triggered the two-year Israeli military assault in Gaza, Reuters reported.

The Israeli military said the strike targeting Yazouri also killed two other commanders. The initial statement did not provide a broader casualty count or identify the other two people. Reuters reported no immediate additional comment from Hamas beyond its confirmation of Yazouri’s death.

The report is developing because military operations and ceasefire diplomacy remain active, and information from the conflict zone can change rapidly. The announced death removes a figure both sides described as important to Hamas’s armed operations while adding another pressure point to negotiations aimed at limiting renewed fighting.
dek: Hamas’s armed wing confirmed Mohammed Abdel Salam al-Yazouri died in Thursday’s strike, which Israel said killed two other commanders.
headline: Israel says Gaza strike killed senior Hamas commander
